IC1: Adults (ages 18-65), current service users, with severe [AND] and enduring mental ill-health, which, for clinical purposes, typically relates to diagnostic categories of bipolar disorder, [OR] severe depression, [OR] or schizophrenia. We use the following definition for SMI:
IC2: - Presence of a psychiatric disorder that requires care [AND] and treatment (so, they are [NOT] NOT in symptom remission)
IC3: - Has severe limitations in social [AND] and community functioning (i.e. they are [NOT] not in functional remission)
IC4: - These problems are [NOT] not transient (e.g. temporary, [OR] one-off) in nature (They are systematic [AND] and long-term)
IC5: - Coordinated care provided by care networks [OR] or teams is needed to implement the treatment plan
